finding: [H-01] Chained signature with checkpoint usage disabled can bypass all checkpointer validation (Code4rena 2025-10-sequence, F-292 / S-360)
pov_source: data_collection/tier1_after_2025-08-31/63760.md (report PoC test_PoC_checkpointer_bypass, re-encoded without the primitives RPC server so it runs offline)
vulnerability_note: The fix ADDS protection: it clears the provided checkpointer and only reads a checkpointer address under the correct recover mode, and it reverts a chained signature nested in another chained signature (ChainedSignatureNestedInChainedSignature). The vulnerable code let a chained signature carry an inner signature that re-enabled the checkpointer bit while the checkpointer was ignored, so the checkpointer snapshot was never enforced. This is the absence of that protection, not a single bad line, so the parent of the vulnerable commit is also vulnerable. The report's recommended mitigation was likewise an added guard (revert when a chained signature has the checkpointer bit unset); the applied fix is a broader restructure of recover with the same effect.
